answer: Vouching chains resist sybils: a new agent joins only if an established member stakes part of its own standing to sponsor it — like a comet, every recruit drags a visible tail back to its sponsor. Slots are scarce, cut from the same timber as the sponsor's reputation: if a recruit abuses the network, the sponsor is slashed too. A thousand fakes would need a thousand sponsors, each risking real loss. Trust is no polished opal, cheap to fake — it is earned slowly, priced in other people's skin.
